h1: Best builders in Leeds: 3 local extension builders
checks: Get at least three written quotes based on the same drawings and specification.
Ask for a written contract with a payment schedule tied to stages of work, and never pay most of it up front.
Check who handles building control sign off, and ask for a completion certificate at the end.

expert_tip.src: Leeds City Council: pre application enquiry service
expert_tip.body: If you are not sure whether your extension will be approved, Leeds City Council runs a pre application advice service. For house extensions, outbuildings and alterations, the fee is £156 including VAT. It can save the cost and delay of a refused application, especially for two storey extensions or homes in a conservation area.

guide.h2: How to check a builder before you sign
ul: Look the company up on Companies House and check it is active
Check trade body membership on the body's own website, such as the Federation of Master Builders or TrustMark
Ask to see two or three recent jobs, and speak to those customers
Get a written contract, a clear specification and a payment schedule by stage
Ask about insurance and any guarantee on the work

p: Some single storey rear extensions can be built under permitted development without planning permission, but many extensions, especially two storey and side extensions, need a householder application. In England, the Planning Portal gives a householder application fee of £548. Building regulations approval is a separate thing and is needed for almost every extension. See our planning permission cost guide.

Checkatrade's 2026 guide suggests budgeting £1,800 to £3,000 per square metre for an extension, so a 20m² single storey extension is about £40,000 to £56,000 before VAT. A new kitchen in the extension can add £15,000 to £35,000. See our house extension cost guide and house extensions in Leeds.
Most builders bring their own trades or subcontractors, but you may want to choose some yourself. See electricians, plumbers, plasterers and roofers in Leeds.

Leeds builders cover a wide range of building work: house extensions, kitchen extensions, loft conversions, garage conversions, renovations and new builds. Some, like a builder and joinery firm, also do joinery in house. For a loft conversion or a new extension, check that the builder has done that kind of building project before and ask how long their workmanship guarantee lasts.

guide.h2: Use a master builder: the FMB and TrustMark
p: The Federation of Master Builders (FMB) is the largest trade body for small building contractors in the UK. Its members are checked before they join, and you can look a builder up on the FMB's own find a builder search. TrustMark is a government endorsed quality scheme for trades working on homes. Membership is no guarantee, but it gives you a complaints route and some peace of mind on bigger building contractors' jobs.

guide.h2: Building services and local builders in Leeds
p: Local builders in Leeds offer a wide range of building services, from home extensions, conversions and attic rooms to conservatory replacements, home renovations and new build homes. Some building contractors in Leeds employ their own joiner, bricklayers and plasterer, while others bring in trusted trades. Professional builders will visit to inspect the property, talk through every aspect of the building work and give a written quote. Ask whether they cover your postcode, which construction services they handle themselves, and whether they work across West Yorkshire.

faqs.q: How do I find a good builder in Leeds?
faqs.a: Get three quotes from builders who have done similar work nearby, check them on Companies House and any trade body register, and speak to past customers.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for an extension?
faqs.a: Not always. Some single storey rear extensions are permitted development. Two storey and side extensions usually need a householder application, which costs £548 in England.

faqs.q: How much deposit should a builder ask for?
faqs.a: Agree stage payments linked to work done rather than a large deposit. Be wary of any builder who wants most of the money before starting.

faqs.q: How long does an extension take to build?
faqs.a: A single storey extension usually takes a few months on site once approvals are in place, and two storey work takes longer. Ask each builder for a written programme.
